speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: All three Motions are scheduled to be dealt with today.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In the normal Order of Business, under the Standing Orders, Motions for leave to introduce Bills would be dealt with before Motions on matters to be debated.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this case, however, the question of whether there is a need to amend the PPIPA to allow Parliament to back pay Mr Iswaran will depend on whether or not Parliament resolves to suspend him in the first place.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: This would be a more logical flow and allow for more efficient conduct of parliamentary business.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Our healthcare and frontline workers had been at the forefront of the battle against COVID-19.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: We have thus invited representative healthcare and frontline workers to attend Parliament when the Motion is moved, so that we can acknowledge their efforts and put on record our gratitude and appreciation to all the healthcare and frontline workers in their presence.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under the current Order of Business in the Order Paper, the commencement time of the Motion is variable, depending on the duration of the speeches and clarifications in the Second Readings of the three Bills.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: It would also likely start only in the evening.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: As such, I am moving to revise the Order of Business as stated earlier, to provide certainty in timetabling and not inconvenience these healthcare and frontline workers, many of whom may have had to take time off to attend.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: In this case, we do have one private Member's Bill standing in the name of Mr Seah Kian Peng and it is currently listed after the Ministry for Home Affair (MHA)'s Online Criminal Harms Bill, which is being taken by Minister Josephine Teo.

speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
text: Under her current travel itinerary, she will only be back tomorrow evening and will only be able to take the Online Criminal Harms Bill on Wednesday at the earliest.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 6.45 pm.

speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 6.26 pm until 6.45 pm.﻿ Sitting resumed at 6.45 pm.
